extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editorial cartoonists, comics journalists, historians, and general readers interested in journalism awards
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the evaluative criteria and descriptive qualities used for the Pulitzer Prize in the category now called Illustrated Reporting and Commentary (formerly Editorial Cartooning). The page lists historic formal characteristics and many winner rationales that describe the qualities the board values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguished editorial cartoon or portfolio
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 1922 the prize had been awarded for a distinguished editorial cartoon or portfolio of cartoons published during the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching eligibility/quality threshold for the award as historically stated on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Work characterized by originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the principal characteristics of award-winning editorial cartoons/portfolios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Work characterized by editorial effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates how effectively the cartoon or illustrated piece communicates an editorial point or commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of drawing
rubrics_metrics.description: Work characterized by quality of drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses the technical drawing skill and visual craft in the submitted cartoons or illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictorial effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Work characterized by pictorial effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers the overall visual impact, composition, and expressive power of the imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguished body of work / service
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarding for distinguished service as a cartoonist or for a body of work (not only single cartoons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pulitzer citations sometimes recognize a cartoonist’s overall contributions during the year or career, not merely a single piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and clarity under daily deadlines (editorial cartooning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial cartoons are quick, in-the-moment commentary that emphasize clarity under daily deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Association of American Editorial Cartoonists contrasted editorial cartoons as requiring fast turnaround and clear messaging on current events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to educate oneself on complex issues and craft well-informed opinions quickly
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial cartoonists must learn complex issues and produce well-informed opinions in a single take.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This highlights the research, synthesis, and speed expected of traditional editorial cartooning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth of reporting and time investment (illustrated reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrated reporting/comics journalism often takes days, weeks, or months to craft a story and can run for pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes illustrated reporting by its longer process, sustained reporting, and longer-form storytelling as opposed to single-panel immediacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinion vs. reporting balance (illustrated reporting may or may not present an opinion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrated reporting may or may not be presenting an opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that the category encompasses both opinionated editorial work and longer-form reportage that can be more documentary or narrative-driven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Cartoons that are perceptive in diagnosing or illuminating issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winner citations praise perceptive cartoons that reveal insights about contemporary topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive style
rubrics_metrics.description: Work executed with a distinctive artistic style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated winner rationales commend a unique or recognizable artistic voice as a positive quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of humor / wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of humor, wit, or biting satire to communicate the work’s point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations reference biting wit, humor, and comic effect as key virtues in effective editorial cartoons and illustrated commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Piercing / sharp commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that delivers piercing, sharp, or trenchant commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many winners are described as producing piercing or sharp perspectives that cut to the heart of an issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freshness / originality of approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistently fresh, original approaches to subject matter and form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pulitzer citations often highlight freshness and originality as distinguishing characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoughtful and powerful messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic work that produces thoughtful, powerful messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates the depth and persuasive strength of the message conveyed by imagery and text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity paired with piercing effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple visual approach that still achieves a piercing or powerful effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some winners are lauded for clarity and power achieved through simple, economical visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of animation / new media forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion and effective use of animation or digital formats in cartoons/illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2010 winner citation and others note innovation in medium (animated cartoons, web presentation) as part of evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed artistry and craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed, careful artistic execution and craftsmanship in the illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations praise detailed artistry as contributing to the work’s persuasive or aesthetic power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to engage readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Cartoons and illustrated pieces that engage readers broadly and powerfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement is measured by the work’s capacity to draw in and move a readership through clarity, humor, or visual power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual and editorial power combined with clarity of communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pulitzer rationales repeatedly emphasize both power (forcefulness) and clarity as desirable qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensive research and factual grounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Work underpinned by extensive research and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially for illustrated reporting, the board highlights extensive research as important (e.g., ability to distill complex issues after research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to distill complex issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Skill in simplifying and clarifying complex topics without losing nuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winner citations commend artists who can make complicated matters accessible through succinct visuals and text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorability (especially in satire/lampooning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that is memorable in its satirical or lampooning effect, particularly on partisan conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited winners are noted for memorable lampooning and sustained satirical impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and range of subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A diverse collection of subjects tackled with range and versatility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some winners are recognized for covering a wide array of topics with equal effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clever ideas and clear point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of clever visual ideas to drive home a clear, unmistakable point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates originality of concept and clarity of the cartoonist’s perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thought-provoking quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that provokes thought and reflection in readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pulitzer citations laud cartoons that stimulate consideration of issues beyond immediate reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong imagery that conveys layered meaning concisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of strong images to connect with readers and convey layers of meaning in few words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conciseness and multi-layered symbolism are positively highlighted in award rationales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sophisticated stylistic techniques (line, color, texture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sophisticated combination of bold line work with subtle colors and textures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical stylistic sophistication in rendering, color choice, and texture is cited as enhancing impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flawless artistry
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemplary, technically flawless artistic execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some winners receive praise for near-perfect craft and execution alongside editorial strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biting prose / crisp writing paired with visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharp, biting prose or captions that complement the visual work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The interplay of text and image—strong writing alongside images—is an evaluative factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional power and human storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotionally powerful storytelling, particularly in graphic narrative form that humanizes subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winner citations for illustrated reportage emphasize emotional resonance and humanization of subjects (e.g., refugees, prisoners).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic narrative storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of comics/graphic narrative form to tell a coherent, emotionally affecting story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes longer-form narrative competence in addition to single-panel editorial work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bravery / daring subject choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Willingness to take on daring, controversial, or risky subject matter, including exposing wrongdoing or injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some winners are cited for tackling issues affecting disenfranchised communities and calling out lies, hypocrisy, and fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirical skewering of personalities and policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Satirical work that skewers personalities and policies effectively, often by juxtaposing style and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pulitzer citations note effective satire even when presented in visually gentle or deceptively sweet styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility — making complex issues understandable to a wider public
rubrics_metrics.description: Using graphics and narrative to make complex or obscure issues accessible to a broad audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited winners are praised for translating complex human-rights or data topics into accessible storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining statistical/data reporting with keen analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration of statistical reporting and data analysis with striking illustrations or graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes excellence in melding data journalism with illustration to clarify large-scale or complex facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visually-driven storytelling that humanizes subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories driven primarily by visuals that humanize individuals (e.g., prisoners, refugees) and their experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates how visuals can center human experience and elicit empathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deftness, creativity, and fearlessness
rubrics_metrics.description: Combination of technical deftness, creative approach, and fearlessness in tackling subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pulitzer citations sometimes group these personal/creative qualities as reasons for awarding the prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of visuals and words to illuminate complex global challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting that uses both visuals and prose to shed light on global issues like surveillance and digital scams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses the integrated use of text and imagery to reveal and explain evolving, complex global phenomena.
